structure_defect_details: Broken seam: the MNLI-100 low-data result is appended to the scatter-plot paragraph with no transition (L73).
Repeated scope: attention-only scope and MLP/LayerNorm/bias future work at L46, restated in limitations at L89.
top_issues: Korean noun frames and formulaic phrasing: "...낫다는 점을 보여 줍니다" (L20), "...시작한다는 점을 확인할 수 있습니다" (L38), ""시사"로 제시한 해석입니다" (L83).
Loose results grouping and repetition: low-data result tacked onto the GPT-3 scatter paragraph (L73); scope/future-work and variance notes repeated between L46/L69 and L89.

A.reason: Y's paper_author matches the paper and it has no editorial table note; X has the L72 omission note and "Microsoft".

B.reason: Y keeps 미세조정 consistently and gives English terms on first use; X mixes 미세조정/파인튜닝. Both have noun frames.

C.reason: X repeats the batching drawback (L52/L92) and has the L72 seam; Y's seams (L73) and repeats (L46/L89) are a little lighter.

D.reason: Both give the same worked parameter count and init rationale; Y adds budget configs, X adds the 1/1536 ratio.

E.reason: Y keeps the full table without a meta note; X's table is fine but its omission note is distracting. Y's display formula omits alpha/r, a small offset.

F.reason: No unsupported or wrong claims in either post (0/22 and 0/24).

G.reason: Both descriptions 120-160 chars, open with LoRA, use TL;DR numbers; use_math correct.

U1.reason: Both cover the full arc; Y adds low-data and training settings, X is equally sufficient.

U2.reason: X is shorter but its TL;DR is four sentences and it repeats a limitation; Y's TL;DR is three sentences but the results run longer.

X1.reason: Both use six long phrase-like tags with one or two paper terms.

preference.reason: Both posts are factually clean (no errors in 22 and 24 checked claims) and cover the same material at the same depth, so the gap is small. Y wins on consistent terminology with English terms on first use, a correct paper_author, a full verbatim table without an editorial note, and fewer repeated facts. X is slightly shorter and has a neat 1/1536 worked ratio, but it mixes 미세조정/파인튜닝, repeats the batching drawback, and inserts a meta note about its own table. A tie on most criteria; Y is the modest overall preference.
